draft.title: Ambiguity
card: A detail is ambiguous when it can be read in more than one way. Two readers can each find a different, reasonable meaning in it.
Ambiguity is not the same as a muddle. A writer can leave a meaning open on purpose, so that the reader has to think about it.
Writers can create it through tone, symbols, connotation (the feelings a word carries) or hints about what is to come.
Example: the story ends with a girl looking at a closed gate and smiling slightly. She may be relieved, or she may be plotting a way through. The text supports both readings.
draft.remember: An ambiguous detail can be read in more than one way, and a writer may do this on purpose.

a.q: Which sentence from a story is the most ambiguous?
opts: Ravi nodded at the offer, but his eyes stayed on the door
Ravi said yes to the offer and shook the man's hand
Ravi refused the offer and walked straight out the door
Ravi took the offer and told everyone he was delighted
a.why: Ravi's nod and his gaze at the door point in different directions, so the reader could take him as agreeing, doubtful or ready to leave. In the other options his action and feelings are stated plainly, so only one reading fits.
a.clue: Look for the detail that points two ways at once.

b.q: A story closes with Mia leaving a sealed envelope on a table and walking away without a word. Why might the writer end it this way?
opts: To let readers decide for themselves what the envelope means
To tell readers exactly what the envelope contains
To show that the writer ran out of ideas for the story
To make sure every reader reaches the same conclusion
b.why: The unexplained envelope can be read in several ways, so the writer leaves the meaning open on purpose and readers must think about it. The idea that the writer simply ran out of ideas is tempting, but ambiguity can be a deliberate choice, not a muddle.
b.clue: Think about what the reader is not told.

a.best: Ravi nodded at the offer, but his eyes stayed on the door

b.best: To let readers decide for themselves what the envelope means
